cases_detail.description: Two clean digital PDFs, submitted in the intended order.
Five digital documents of varying length in one packet.
Documents submitted out of order, reordered by filename.
Filename ordering must be case-insensitive and stable.
Documents arrive in arbitrary order and are organized by caller-supplied semantic labels, with repeatable sections kept stable.
Letter, A4, and legal pages merged into one packet.
Digital pages rotated 90 and 270 degrees.
A 40-page packet, to stress page conservation through the merge.
Sparse but genuinely digital text, near the scanned-detection threshold of 40 characters per page.
One scanned document alongside a digital one; OCR should hit only it.
An entirely scanned packet, the common paper-office case.
A scan fed through the feeder crooked; deskew should recover it.
A speckled photocopy, the usual cause of OCR garbage.
A 72 dpi scan, below what OCR reliably reads.
A scan fed in sideways, then OCRed.
Separator sheets with no content. OCR cannot add text, so the packet should still be produced and the emptiness reported rather than silently passed.
A heavily speckled photocopy at 5% noise. OCR cannot read it; the packet must come back flagged rather than quietly unsearchable.
A page fed in at 25 degrees, well past what deskew recovers.
6pt print at fax resolution, below what OCR resolves.
A 50 dpi scan, which the OCR stage rejects outright. Refusing the job is the correct answer; returning a packet that claims to be searchable is not.
